newsitem.title: TURKEY: Iraqi Kurd refugees to fly to Guam temporarily.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi Kurd refugees to fly to Guam temporarily.

text.p: Hundreds of Iraqi Kurds who worked for U.S. military and civilian groups in northern Iraq will be flown to the Pacific island of Guam over the next few days en route to the United States, a U.S. diplomat said on Monday.
"They will go from here to the island of Guam. On the island of Guam there is a U.S. air force base," U.S. diplomat Frank Ricciardoni told reporters in Diyarbakir airport.
"There they will be taken care of, given food and medical care. They will be (flown) as refugees into the United States. This will take probably two or three months."
The diplomat said the first group of refugees, who crossed over to Turkey from northern Iraq on Sunday, would leave for Guam on Tuesday on a chartered aircraft.
"These people are U.S. government employees and their families. They are around 300, but with their families they number about 2,500," Ricciardoni said.

More than 300 refugees -- the first group to leave for Guam -- had already travelled to the main southeastern city of Diyarbakir on Monday from a camp in the Turkish border town of Silopi, where the Kurds were first located after leaving Iraq.

Most of the refugees worked as employees of U.S. aid programmes and the U.S.-led air operation patrolling a no-fly zone for Iraqi aircraft in northern Iraq. But some are believed to have been engaged in intelligence activities for the Americans.

The Kurds had been holed up in small hotels and private residences waiting to escape since Iraqi troops helped the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) faction take the city of Arbil from a rival group on August 31.
The KDP, led by Massoud Barzani, went on to conquer most of northern Iraq and boost Saddam's control of a region where he had been ineffective for the past five years.
U.S. citizens in government programmes in Iraqi Kurdistan were evacuated shortly after the fall of Arbil.
